facts.t: Electoral bonds funded most of the Congress's 2024 donations
facts.d: 73% of Congress donations and 43% of the BJP's came through the scheme before the Supreme Court struck it down in February 2024 for violating Article 19(1)(a) and enabling corporate quid pro quo.

facts.t: The government replaced the Chief Justice on the ECI selection panel
facts.d: Anoop Baranwal (2023) had prescribed a collegium including the Chief Justice of India. The CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023 substituted a Union Cabinet Minister — a change now under challenge in Jaya Thakur v. UoI.

facts.t: 72% of the BJP's 2023-24 funds came from unknown sources
facts.d: Disclosure is mandatory only above ₹20,000. Corporate donations made up 88.9% of national parties' funding that year, with the BJP receiving ₹2,064.5 crore — roughly nine times all other parties combined.

bank.q: The Model Code of Conduct derives its authority from:
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Election Commission's plenary powers under Article 324
bank.e: Article 324. The MCC has no statutory backing at all, which is why granting it statutory status is the leading reform proposal.

bank.q: With reference to the Election Commission, consider the following statements:
s: It registers political parties under section 29A of the RoPA.
It advises the President or Governor on the disqualification of legislators.
It has direct administrative control over the staff who conduct elections.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The ECI depends on state government staff, which is why control over election machinery features among the reforms sought.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding):
pairs: 2. The CEC is first among equals
3. A person in lawful custody is barred from voting and from contesting
4. Voters have a right under Article 19(1)(a) to know candidates' antecedents
bank.e: Seshan on the CEC's status, ADR on disclosure, PUCL on NOTA, and Jan Chaukidar on custody.

bank.q: Which one of the following was NOT a change made by the Finance Act, 2017?
o: Removal of the cap on corporate donations
Removal of the requirement to disclose corporate donations
Introduction of the Electoral Bond Scheme
Amendment of FCRA to permit foreign-owned Indian companies to donate
bank.e: That FCRA change came through the Finance Act, 2016, a year earlier.

bank.as: The electoral bond scheme was struck down in February 2024.
bank.rs: It violated the voter's right to information under Article 19(1)(a) and enabled corporate quid pro quo.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the right to know candidates' and parties' funding sources traces back to UoI v. ADR.

bank.q: Consider the following electoral reforms already undertaken:
s: Lowering the voting age to eighteen through the 61st Amendment.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are done. State funding remains a proposal — recommended in part by the Indrajit Gupta Committee and in full, conditionally, by the Law Commission.

bank.q: The Law Commission's 1999 recommendation on state funding made it contingent on:
o: Bringing parties under the RTI Act
bank.e: Full state funding contingent on internal party democracy. The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) had recommended partial state funding.

bank.q: All of the following are identified weaknesses of the ECI EXCEPT:
o: Perceived partisanship arising from executive control over appointments
Weak enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct
Absence of any power to countermand a poll
bank.e: The ECI can countermand or cancel polls in cases of mass rigging — one of its strongest powers.

bank.q: With reference to the Model Code of Conduct, consider the following prohibitions:
s: Announcing new schemes, grants or construction promises during elections.
Appeals to caste or communal sentiment.
bank.e: All three are prohibited, though enforcement depends entirely on the ECI's moral authority rather than statutory penalty.

bank.q: Which reform is proposed to capture spending that currently escapes candidate expenditure limits?
o: Amending section 77 of the RoPA to include all third-party expenses
bank.e: Third-party and party expenditure on a candidate's behalf currently falls outside the section 77 accounting.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about electoral trusts:
s: Prudent Electoral Trust donated to both the BJP and the Congress.
Triumph Electoral Trust donated exclusively to the BJP.
Electoral trusts are barred from disclosing their donors.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Electoral trusts are required to disclose contributions — it was electoral bonds that guaranteed anonymity.

bank.as: Removal proceedings against a Chief Election Commissioner were initiated for the first time in Indian history.
bank.rs: The CEC enjoys the same removal protection as a Supreme Court judge.
bank.e: Both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion — it explains why such proceedings must take the impeachment route, not why they were initiated. The proceedings were unsuccessful.
